name: Game-Like Website
philosophy: The visitor learns by playing. One bounded mechanic turns the message into something you do, and the explainer holds the same content for anyone who skips.
principles: Completion leads to the call to action
visualIdentity: A small invented world with its own rules, characters or tokens, with an interface styled as part of the game.
artDirection: Build a coherent little world: consistent sprite or shape language, sound on demand, score and progress as design elements.

layout.composition: A stage section that dominates, then the explainer below with the same items in readable form.

typography: Characterful display type that fits the world; plain body type in the explainer.
colour: A saturated, world-specific palette, with enough contrast for play.
contentPresentation: Content unlocks as items in the game, each with a short title and text mirrored in the explainer.
assets: Authored sprites or shapes; licensed sound; everything recorded in the register.
animation: Game physics and feedback: collect, unlock, celebrate. Keyboard and touch both work.
scrolling: Scrolling is paused only while the visitor is actively playing and focus is on the stage.
responsive: Touch controls and a smaller stage on mobile; fallback to the explainer on weak devices.
useCases: Only when the client confirms play is the point
avoidFor: Any brief where play is not the point

fromTeam: Workbook: no tools, demo or evidence yet
Skill: one bounded mechanic with progress, sound and skip
interpreted: All design guidance: no team evidence yet
